record.paper_title: Crystal Nucleation in Liquids: Open Questions and Future Challenges in Molecular Dynamics Simulations
record.original_question: How can heterogeneous crystal nucleation be simulated atomistically for increasingly realistic interfaces, including the interfacial detail needed for reliable force fields, while still extracting general trends that are not tied to a single material system?

evidence.quote: In light of the literature we have reviewed in here, we believe that much of the effort has to be devoted in the future to i) enable atomistic simulations of heterogeneous nucleation dealing with increasingly realistic interfaces and to ii) obtain general, maybe non material-specific trends able to point the community into the right direction, even at the cost of sacrificing accuracy to a certain extent.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop an atomistic molecular-dynamics simulation framework for heterogeneous crystal nucleation in a supercooled liquid in contact with a solid substrate that simultaneously achieves the following two objectives:

(1) Realistic interfaces. Construct and simulate liquid–substrate systems with progressively more realistic interfacial structure (e.g., chemically and geometrically detailed substrates including surface terminations, defects, steps, roughness, and adsorbates), and specify the level of interfacial detail (atomic positions, bonding, polarization, charge transfer, etc.) that an interatomic force field must capture in order to yield quantitatively reliable nucleation rates, critical-nucleus sizes, and free-energy barriers ΔG* under classical nucleation theory of the form
J = J0 exp(−ΔG*/kBT),
where ΔG* depends on the liquid–crystal surface tension, the chemical-potential difference, and a substrate-dependent shape factor f(θ) ∈ [0,1].

(2) Material-transferable trends. Identify, from such simulations, general scaling laws or qualitative trends relating nucleation behavior (induction times, nucleation rates, contact angles of the critical nucleus, polymorph selection) to coarse interfacial descriptors (lattice mismatch, surface energy, wettability, topography length scale) that hold across distinct material systems rather than being tied to a single substrate–liquid pair, even if some quantitative accuracy is sacrificed.

Provide a methodology that meets both (1) and (2), together with criteria validating that the extracted trends are genuinely material-nonspecific.
artifact.status_search_result: Heterogeneous nucleation at realistic interfaces remains an active research challenge in molecular simulation, with no consensus framework that simultaneously delivers fully realistic interfacial force fields and material-transferable trends; reviews and recent simulation studies continue to list this as an open methodological problem.

status_evidence.title: Crystal Nucleation in Liquids: Open Questions and Future Challenges
status_evidence.snippet: Future effort must enable atomistic simulations of heterogeneous nucleation with increasingly realistic interfaces and obtain general, possibly non material-specific trends.
status_evidence.claim: The challenge is explicitly framed as open and forward-looking.
